rulings: CF-CARDNUMBER-ALONE-IS-NOT-IDENTITY. CPA-DT names FOUR cards in 2025: Diego Tornes (bowman-chrome), Devin Taylor (bowman-draft), Drew Thorpe (topps-chrome-platinum) and Dallas Turner (football topps-chrome). The number decides nothing; the player the title names decides the product.

CF-A-COLLISION-SALE-WITH-A-READABLE-PLAYER-GOES-TO-THAT-PLAYERS-ROW (Drew, 2026-09-05). Identity is read from the TITLE first and the stored playerName only as a fallback; a row with neither PARKS. Measured here: zero rows park.

THE POPULATION IS ADDRESSED TWO WAYS, AND A SLUG-ONLY SCAN MISSES HALF OF IT. sold_comps is partitioned on /cardId, but 584 of the 1,044 CPA-DT rows sit in VENDOR-ID partitions (cardhedge/cardsight) whose cardId is not a slug at all. Their identity lives in hobbyiqCardId, which is what the pricing engine reads. Those rows are REPOINTED in place, never relocated: their partition is not a card address and must not become one.

THE TITLE IS THE EVIDENCE, THE STORED FIELD IS NOT. 12 rows carry a dirty playerName ('Draft Devin Taylor', 'Devin Taylor Oakland', 'Devin Taylor On Caes', 'Devin Taylor Au') and one is flatly wrong ('Diego Tornes' on a title reading 'Devin Taylor 2025 Bowman Chrome Draft 1st Auto Oakland Athletics'). repair-cpa-draft-refile folds playerName EXACTLY, so those rows read as to-key-checklist-does-not-name-this-player and were left in the wrong pool. The companion code change lets the row's own words corroborate a checklist claim when the exact fold cannot.

A DESTINATION MUST BE CHECKLIST-BACKED. Every destination in `entries` was confirmed to exist in card_catalog with a checklist source. Destinations that do not exist are recorded in `deferred` and NOT routed — a repair never mints an identity from a sale. Several are parallels the slug spells but no checklist names ('blue-wave', 'gold-ink', 'purple', 'yellow', a bare 'refractor' with no print run, and the malformed 'refractor-auto-499').
THE PRINT RUN AND THE PARALLEL NEVER MOVE. Every entry changes segment 4 (the product) and nothing else.
